extraction.Name: Charles Janis
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent to his 160 acre allotment at the time it was issued; but that he was informed by the Indian Agency, if he did not take it over, it would be assessed for taxes, and finally sold for them; so he accepted the patent
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: in 1920, he deeded his allotment to his brother, John Janis, who was to sell it, and give deponent $2000.00 for it
extraction.Buyer: John Janis did sell it to Joe Harris, of Denby, South Dakota, but did not pay any money over to deponent, did not even tell him how much he received for it, so that the allotment was a total loss to deponent
extraction.Occupation/Income: trucks for the United States Government, between Pine Ridge, South Dakota, and Rushville, Nebraska; and that this work is his only source of income
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent; has good health; single, and no one but himself to support; has never received any help from the County, State nor the United States Government; allotment was 160 acres | TASK 5 CAT_3 BACKFILL 2026-05-04 (patents database): Allotment 70 sourced from federal-register-app patents database (Christian's research, 2026-05-04).
